method_claim: Observational questions and context confounding
exact_protocol: We used an observational cross-dataset design to compare Fake and Real health information in two dataset contexts. CoAID News represented a COVID-focused sensitive-period/context collection; FakeHealth HealthStory provided a non-COVID health-information comparator. The primary engagement question was how the within-dataset Fake/Real observed-post engagement ratio differed between these contexts. The supporting text question was how well learned Fake/Real textual associations generalized from one context to the other. Dataset identity and period/context were not independently varied, so the design did not estimate a causal effect of a COVID period.

method_claim: Distinct analytical branches and external target
exact_protocol: The engagement and text branches addressed distinct outcomes. Engagement analyses modeled captured social-post counts associated with content entities. Text analyses predicted the datasets' analytical Fake/Real labels from prepared text, using within-context evaluation and transfer between datasets. Engagement measurements were not text predictors, and no mediation analysis linked lexical associations to sharing. Independent COVID-Rumor NEWS validation compared CoAID-source and FakeHealth-source classifiers on a common COVID-focused target.

method_claim: Primary and robustness roles
exact_protocol: CoAID Specification A and natural combined-text Logistic Regression were the primary protocols for their respective branches. Alternative entity specifications, Linear SVM, title-only text, publisher-held-out evaluation, and DistilRoBERTa were robustness analyses with separately stated evaluation scopes. Dataset-specific labels and reference populations were retained throughout. We used the final validated cohorts and split assignments rather than combining results from different stages of cohort preparation.

method_claim: CoAID releases, News labels, linkage, and final entity counts
exact_protocol: CoAID inputs comprised the official dated release directories `05-01-2020`, `07-01-2020`, `09-01-2020`, and `11-01-2020`. We used the News subset for the primary analyses. Fake/Real labels came from the original News filenames. Content records were linked within their release and file category to post mappings through the original content ID and to reply mappings through the news ID. Release-local numeric IDs were not treated as globally unique identifiers. The engagement sample under Specification A contained 5,337 analytical entities: 922 Fake and 4,415 Real.

method_claim: HealthStory review threshold, linkage, counts, and retweet exclusion
exact_protocol: FakeHealth HealthStory was the primary comparator; HealthRelease was not part of the reported primary comparison. The original expert-review rating defined Fake when the score was below 3 and Real when the score was at least 3. Reviews, available article content, and engagement mappings were joined by the original news ID. The engagement sample contained 1,690 items, comprising 472 Fake and 1,218 Real. Its primary post outcome used the mapping's tweet IDs. Separate retweet mappings were excluded from the common outcome because an equivalent CoAID mapping was unavailable.

method_claim: COVID-Rumor NEWS labels, unit, exclusions, and distinct label semantics
exact_protocol: COVID-Rumor contributed only its NEWS subset for external text evaluation. The item-level T/F/U labels mapped T to Real and F to Fake; unverified entries were excluded. Each item contributed one statement, with associated website records used for overlap screening rather than as additional text observations. The Twitter subset was excluded. These mappings aligned analytical label orientation without equating FakeHealth review quality, CoAID labels, and COVID-Rumor veracity annotations. FakeNewsNet did not contribute to the quantitative analyses described here.

subsection: 2.3 CoAID entity resolution and analytical unit
method_claim: Specific-resource identity and prohibited merge shortcuts
exact_protocol: CoAID release records can represent repeated captures of a specific resource, updates to that resource, or unresolved identities. We applied the validated version-aware entity rules before counting engagement. Repeated release membership alone was insufficient to identify the same content version, particularly for maintained institutional guidance and surveillance pages. Resource identity relied on the audited item-specific URL/resource mapping and source lineage. Shared domains, generic titles, branding, boilerplate, and social overlap did not create content-identity merges.

subsection: 2.3 CoAID entity resolution and analytical unit
method_claim: Primary conservative Specification A
exact_protocol: Primary Specification A collapsed captures with high-confidence evidence of the same content or only minor updates. Material updates were divided according to the validated version partitions. Captures with insufficient evidence of content stability remained separate, as did unresolved cross-URL records. This conservative rule avoided assuming equivalence when the available excerpts could not establish it. Original singleton observations were retained without claiming that their historical content stability had been verified. The resulting analytical unit could therefore be a validated content version or a separately retained capture with explicit uncertainty flags.

subsection: 2.3 CoAID entity resolution and analytical unit
method_claim: Multifield version evidence and complete-link partitioning
exact_protocol: Version decisions combined available body, title, abstract, and metadata evidence. Identical informative content and compatible metadata supported sameness or minor updates; material-change decisions required corroborating evidence across fields. Missing, error, boilerplate, and uncorroborated excerpt differences remained uncertain. Source-title changes or dates alone did not establish material change. Approved material-version partitions used complete-link pair checks, preventing a chain of pairwise links from joining mutually incompatible captures. [Supplementary Methods S1](supplementary_methods_notes.md#s1-content-identity-lineage-and-engagement-linkage) identifies the audit artifacts defining these decisions.

subsection: 2.3 CoAID entity resolution and analytical unit
method_claim: Sensitivity specifications, lineage, and unique ID unions
exact_protocol: Specification B additionally assumed stability for insufficient-evidence captures within the same validated specific resource, while still separating material versions and unresolved cross-URL captures. Specification C excluded the audited insufficient-version and unresolved-identity captures. Both were sensitivity populations. Stable entity identifiers, original source UIDs, release/file/row references, member captures, uncertainty flags, and exclusions were preserved. Within each legitimate entity, social counts were reconstructed from unique ID unions. Splitting entities could expose shared social IDs across entities; those memberships were retained for dependence modeling rather than deleted.

method_claim: Unique observed-post outcome and measurement scope
exact_protocol: The primary outcome was the number of unique observed posts per analytical content entity, including entities with zero observed posts. CoAID counts used the union of linked post IDs across an entity's member captures; FakeHealth counts used unique tweet IDs in its item mapping. Repeated IDs within an entity were counted once. These outcomes measured captured engagement/sharing, without an exposure denominator, complete diffusion cascades, or reconstructed follower/network topology. Historical deletions, private activity, and uncaptured posts remained outside the measurement.

method_claim: Observed overlap graph and bootstrap clusters
exact_protocol: We constructed a separate overlap graph for each dataset and CoAID specification. Nodes were analytical entities, and an edge joined two entities when they shared a counted post ID or a counted reply ID. Connected components, including singleton nodes, defined dependence clusters for resampling. Graph construction preserved the analytical units and their observed counts. FakeHealth retweets excluded from the primary outcome were also excluded from this graph. A connected component was a dependence unit, not a claim that its members represented identical content.

method_claim: Dominant-component sensitivity and secondary outcomes
exact_protocol: CoAID's dominant overlap component motivated a specified influence analysis excluding that component. Remaining entities defined the sensitivity population and its standardization distribution. The graph captured dependence evidenced by shared observed IDs; common publishers or resources without such IDs could introduce additional dependence. Reply counts and engagement-occurrence summaries were secondary diagnostics. The occurrence of any post used by the post hurdle was distinguished from a broader indicator of any post or reply.

method_claim: Dataset-specific count families and covariate designs
exact_protocol: We modeled CoAID post counts using a hurdle model with a logistic component for any observed post and a genuine zero-truncated negative-binomial NB2 component for positive counts. Both components included the Fake/Real indicator and first-recorded-release fixed effects, with the May release as reference. First-recorded release described dataset capture provenance rather than a verified publication or exposure time. FakeHealth post counts used an NB2 model with the Fake/Real indicator. No exposure offset or additional text covariate was introduced.

method_claim: Model selection and fixed family during resampling
exact_protocol: The different model structures reflected the datasets' observed count distributions and within-dataset model assessment. For CoAID, the validated rule retained a numerically stable hurdle when it improved AIC over NB2 by more than 2, or when NB2 was unstable. Comparisons used the same full outcome and counted all hurdle parameters. FakeHealth retained NB2 as its primary model. Fits were checked for convergence, gradients, Hessian behavior, and parameter bounds. Model-family selection was held fixed during resampling.

method_claim: Standardized expected-count ratio definition
exact_protocol: We compared standardized expected counts rather than coefficients from these different models. Let m_d(a, X_i) be the fitted expected count for entity i in dataset d with its Fake indicator set to a, retaining its other covariates. For each dataset, we defined

method_claim: Equation for standardized Fake/Real ratio
Hurdle expectation definition
exact_protocol: For the CoAID hurdle, the expected row mean was

method_claim: Equation for full hurdle expected mean
exact_protocol:
$$
m_d(a,X_i)=P(Y_i>0\mid a,X_i)\,E(Y_i\mid Y_i>0,a,X_i).
$$

method_claim: Rowwise averaging, reference distributions, and contrast
exact_protocol: The row-level products were averaged before forming the ratio. We did not substitute the positive-count coefficient or multiply separately averaged component predictions. Each dataset retained its own empirical covariate distribution, including zero-count entities. The cross-context estimand was C = R_CoAID / R_FakeHealth, equivalently theta = log(R_CoAID) − log(R_FakeHealth). Values of C below 1 indicate a smaller Fake/Real observed-post ratio in CoAID; the contrast does not require equivalent model coefficients or a shared reference population.

method_claim: Component resampling, successful refits, and failures
exact_protocol: Uncertainty used an unstratified pairs bootstrap of overlap components. For a dataset with K components, each draw sampled K components with replacement, including all entities whenever their component was selected. Repeated component selections repeated their rows. The chosen model was refitted and re-standardized over that draw's empirical covariate distribution. The protocol targeted 1,000 successful finite post-ratio refits per dataset/specification. Failed attempts were recorded and excluded from percentile summaries; retry rules used the same sampled data. Seed 42 governed reproducible resampling.

method_claim: Independent marginal Cartesian distribution and percentile intervals
exact_protocol: For the cross-context contrast, we combined all ordered pairs of the independently generated CoAID and FakeHealth ratio draws. The 1,000-by-1,000 Cartesian combination formed an equally weighted empirical distribution of log differences and exponentiated ratios. Its 1,000,000 values shared marginal draws and were not independent bootstrap samples. We used linear empirical quantiles for 95% percentile intervals; point estimates remained ratios of fitted standardized ratios. The procedure assumed independence across datasets and did not encompass uncertainty from missing links, model-family selection, or entity resolution. B/C specifications and dominant-component exclusion assessed specified sensitivities separately.

subsection: 2.6 Text cohort construction and leakage control
method_claim: Prepared text and availability/quality rules
exact_protocol: Text cohorts were derived from HealthStory items and CoAID Specification A entities. Preparation normalized whitespace and obvious null placeholders while retaining case, punctuation, URLs, and available language. Natural `combined_text` joined usable title and body fields with a blank line, permitting a title-only or body-only item when the other field was unavailable. Empty or obvious artifact-only records were ineligible. A subsequent label-blind quality audit excluded artifact-dominated content and reviewed title provenance for potential disclosure of the review label. Substantive headlines with poor bodies could remain eligible for combined-text modeling while being excluded from body-only analyses.

subsection: 2.6 Text cohort construction and leakage control
method_claim: Final eligible counts, predictor restrictions, and masking
exact_protocol: The final `primary_modeling_eligible` cohorts contained 1,647 FakeHealth items, with 459 Fake and 1,188 Real, and 3,577 CoAID entities, with 825 Fake and 2,752 Real. Modeling used Fake=1 and Real=0. Natural title/body text was the predictor input; IDs, ratings, source/review metadata, quality flags, engagement, lineage, and split assignments were excluded from predictors. The quality audit retained original strings and exclusion reasons. A separate masked representation replaced known explicit source identifiers using a label-blind dictionary derived from prepared metadata, including evaluation metadata; this was a declared transductive sensitivity, not a training-only source-discovery procedure.

subsection: 2.6 Text cohort construction and leakage control
method_claim: Resource and text leakage barriers
exact_protocol: Leakage groups were connected components of resource identity, source-member/review lineage, and exact or very-high-similarity title/body matches. CoAID versions of a resource remained together, and unresolved identity contexts received conservative grouping without being declared the same entity. Exact generic-template matches could also join evaluation groups. Publisher identity or broad topic alone did not define the primary groups. Label-blind lexical-overlap screening was also performed across datasets; no flagged cross-dataset overlap affected the final modeling cohorts. Thresholds and normalization rules are documented in [Supplementary Methods S3](supplementary_methods_notes.md#s3-text-grouping-quality-and-source-masking).

subsection: 2.6 Text cohort construction and leakage control
method_claim: Grouped holdout/CV selection and preserved assignments
exact_protocol: Rows were sorted by stable UID. Seed-42 StratifiedGroupKFold generated candidate outer partitions, and the holdout fold was selected by closeness to 20% of the total and each class, using counts rather than model outcomes. Five grouped CV folds were formed within the remaining training pool. Final quality filtering preserved those assignments. The modeling-ready training/holdout sizes were 1,317/330 for FakeHealth and 2,875/702 for CoAID. Groups never crossed a fitted training, validation, or test partition, and holdouts never entered tuning. CoAID's short stored excerpts and FakeHealth's longer article bodies remained distinct information budgets.

subsection: 2.7 Classical text models and within-context evaluation
method_claim: LR feature preprocessing and 24-configuration grid
exact_protocol: The primary text classifier was a pipeline of word TF-IDF and Logistic Regression (LR). The vectorizer lowercased text, used Unicode word tokens of at least two characters, sublinear term frequency, smoothed inverse document frequency, L2 normalization, and float64 sparse features. Accent stripping was disabled and maximum document frequency was 1.0. The 24-configuration grid crossed unigram versus unigram-plus-bigram features, minimum document frequency 2 versus 5, C of 0.1, 1, or 10, and unweighted versus balanced classes. LR used L2 regularization, the liblinear solver, tolerance 1e-4, maximum 5,000 iterations, and seed 42.

subsection: 2.7 Classical text models and within-context evaluation
method_claim: Fold-local fitting, selection, and LR tie policy
exact_protocol: Every CV fit learned a fresh vocabulary and IDF from its training fold only. Selection maximized unweighted mean macro F1 across the five saved folds. Means within 0.001 of the best were tied; among them, sample SDs within 0.001 of the lowest were tied. Remaining preferences were unigrams, smaller C, unweighted classes, larger minimum document frequency, and stable configuration ID. Nonconverged configurations were ineligible. The selected natural-text settings were locked before holdout prediction; final within-context fits used only the training pool. Masked-text fits used the corresponding natural configuration without retuning.

subsection: 2.7 Classical text models and within-context evaluation
method_claim: SVM grid, solver, and distinct tie policy
exact_protocol: Linear SVM assessed classifier-choice robustness using the same natural cohorts, splits, and TF-IDF settings. Its 32-configuration grid added C=0.01 to the LR grid. LinearSVC used L2 penalty, squared-hinge loss, `dual="auto"`, tolerance 1e-4, maximum 20,000 iterations, and seed 42. Its tie rule matched LR through the unweighted-class preference, then used configuration ID without the extra minimum-document-frequency preference. Full settings and selected configurations are listed in [Supplementary Methods S4](supplementary_methods_notes.md#s4-classical-tuning-and-selected-settings).

subsection: 2.7 Classical text models and within-context evaluation
method_claim: Fixed thresholds, score types, metrics, and dummy baselines
exact_protocol: LR classified Fake at probability >=0.5; SVM classified Fake at decision score >=0. ROC-AUC and non-interpolated average precision used Fake probabilities for LR and raw decision scores for SVM. We reported macro F1, class-specific performance, balanced accuracy, confusion counts, and ranking measures. SVM scores were not treated as calibrated probabilities. Training-only most-frequent and seed-42 stratified dummy classifiers provided baseline references for the LR evaluation.

method_claim: Frozen source selection and full-source transfer fitting
exact_protocol: Transfer used both directions: FakeHealth to CoAID and CoAID to FakeHealth. Hyperparameters remained those selected using the source dataset's training-pool CV. After within-context evaluation, each source pipeline was refitted on all eligible source rows, including its former holdout. Vocabulary and IDF were learned exclusively from source text. Target items were transformed without fitting, calibration, or threshold tuning. Both source configurations were locked before evaluation, and transfer predictions were frozen before target outcome labels were joined for scoring. Reverse-direction results did not modify the opposite source model.

method_claim: All-target and identical target-holdout comparisons
exact_protocol: We reported all-eligible target performance and performance on the saved target holdout. The latter was primary for transfer-minus-within comparisons because both scores referred to identical target UIDs. Within-context comparators remained the saved training-pool-to-holdout models; only evaluation rows, not training populations or sample sizes, were matched. Natural and masked LR transfer used their corresponding within-target representations. Existing overlap flags and group safeguards were retained rather than redefining target cohorts in response to performance.

method_claim: Frozen within-context LR lexical audit and cutoffs
exact_protocol: Lexical alignment used the frozen natural within-context LR models, not the subsequent full-source transfer fits. We intersected their unigram vocabularies, yielding 4,174 shared terms, with positive coefficients oriented toward Fake. FakeHealth bigrams were excluded from the intersection but remained part of its fitted model. We summarized signed Pearson and Spearman correlations, sign agreement, and sign reversal, defined by a negative coefficient product. Exact-zero cases were accounted for separately. Prespecified subsets comprised all shared terms, terms exceeding either model's shared-vocabulary median absolute coefficient, and the top 1,000, 500, and 100 by maximum absolute coefficient, with lexical tie-breaking.

method_claim: Conditional coefficient interpretation and descriptive scope
exact_protocol: Coefficients were dataset-specific conditional associations, affected by feature space, IDF, correlated predictors, and regularization. They were neither rescaled to a common effect-size unit nor interpreted as causal effects. Alignment summaries were descriptive; no inferential significance test attributed transfer degradation to coefficient reversals.

method_claim: Title-only independent tuning and matched target rows
exact_protocol: Title-only LR used the existing `title_only_modeling_eligible` flags and unchanged resource-group assignments. Each dataset was tuned independently on source training folds using the same LR grid and tie policy. Within-context fits used the eligible training pool; transfer refits used all eligible source titles. Combined-versus-title transfer comparisons restricted evaluation to the identical title-eligible target rows. Masked-title sensitivities used the audited masked field with locked natural-title hyperparameters. Source eligibility and separately selected configurations could differ between representations, so this design did not isolate text length alone.

method_claim: Conservative publisher proxies and complete FakeHealth cohort
exact_protocol: Publisher families were constructed conservatively from prepared names, article hosts, specific URLs, and audited aliases. Normalization did not use labels or article text. Hosted tenants and explicit platform-account identities remained distinct; missing or unresolved sources were not grouped into a single publisher. Connected components combined publisher-family and original resource/leakage barriers. The FakeHealth experiment retained all 1,647 modeling-ready items across 49 observed publisher families and 49 publisher/resource components. These were source proxies rather than a complete corporate-ownership classification.

method_claim: Nested grouped publisher evaluation and masked locks
exact_protocol: Outer evaluation used three-fold StratifiedGroupKFold with shuffling and seed 42. Each outer-training partition received nested publisher/component-aware inner tuning with three folds; the protocol permitted two only if three were infeasible, but all final outer partitions used three. The LR grid and tie rule were unchanged. Each selected configuration was locked before outer prediction and refitted only on its outer-training data. Source-masked fits reused those settings. Outer-fold mean/sample SD, ranges, and pooled classification summaries were distinguished; ROC-AUC was summarized within folds. Comparison with the resource-grouped CV baseline was descriptive and unpaired.

method_claim: Explicit CoAID publisher/class feasibility asymmetry
exact_protocol: No equivalent clean CoAID publisher-held-out language-generalization claim was made. Its identified families were predominantly class-exclusive, mixed-label-family support was sparse, and excluding unresolved publisher rows disproportionately removed Fake items. These feasibility constraints were retained explicitly rather than substituting a restricted CoAID population and treating it as equivalent to the FakeHealth experiment.

method_claim: Pinned checkpoint, pair packing, caps, and truncation asymmetry
exact_protocol: We used `distilbert/distilroberta-base` at immutable revision `fb53ab8802853c8e4fbdbcd0529f21fc6f459b2b`, instantiated as AutoModelForSequenceClassification with two labels. Only prepared title and body text entered the encoder. The validated pair-packing procedure preserved the full title, reserved four official special tokens, and filled the remaining budget with a body prefix. Dynamic padding was applied within each microbatch. Primary maximum sequence length was 512 tokens; the sensitivity cap was 256. The tokenization audit showed substantial FakeHealth truncation and no CoAID truncation at 512, so model-family comparisons did not imply equal available text.

method_claim: Weighted loss, accumulation, and optimizer settings
exact_protocol: Training used FP32 on Apple Silicon MPS in the separate Python 3.12 transformer environment. Microbatch size was 2, with gradient accumulation of 8 and an effective batch size of 16. Weighted cross-entropy used class weight N_train/(2N_train,c), computed only from the labels of that fit's source-training rows. Gradients were normalized by the sum of training class weights within each effective batch, including a final partial batch. AdamW used weight decay 0.01 except for bias and LayerNorm weights, betas (0.9, 0.999), epsilon 1e-8, and gradient-norm clipping at 1.0. The learning-rate schedule was constant with zero warmup.

method_claim: Source grouped CV grid, tie policy, and selected configuration
exact_protocol: Source-only selection used the same five grouped training folds and reserved holdouts as the classical models. Candidate learning rates were 2e-5 and 5e-5; candidate epoch counts were 2 and 3. Each learning-rate trajectory ran for three epochs with validation at epochs 2 and 3. Within 0.001 of the best mean macro F1, selection preferred lower sample SD, fewer epochs, then lower learning rate. Both datasets selected 2e-5 and three epochs. Configurations were locked before holdout and transfer evaluation. No early stopping, mixed precision, oversampling, or target threshold tuning was used.

method_claim: Within/source-transfer populations and locked budget sensitivity
exact_protocol: Within-context final models trained on the source training pool. Transfer models started from the pinned pretrained checkpoint and trained on all eligible source rows, including the former source holdout. Target data remained transform-only; probability >=0.5 defined Fake. Both all-eligible and matched target-holdout scopes were reported. The 256-token sensitivity reused each source's selected learning rate and epoch count, without retuning or changing cohort assignments.

method_claim: Targeted paired budget/seed follow-up
exact_protocol: A targeted FakeHealth-to-CoAID follow-up paired the 256- and 512-token protocols across seeds 42, 123, and 2026. Seed 42 reused the original saved evaluations; the additional seeds repeated full-FakeHealth-source fitting with fixed settings. CoAID's unpadded target token sequences were identical at both caps, while the available FakeHealth source body prefix changed. Paired metric differences, means, sample SDs, ranges, and prediction agreement described budget/seed variability in this direction. This was a stability check rather than a new hyperparameter search or replacement primary protocol.

method_claim: NEWS schema, binary label gate, and predictor restrictions
exact_protocol: The headerless NEWS item table was interpreted using its documented rumor-ID, label, statement-content, and sentiment columns. Only verified binary T/F items were eligible; U and U(Twitter) markers were excluded. Associated website/repost records supplied URLs for screening, not additional observations or predictors. No Twitter-subset files or repost text entered the analysis. IDs, sentiment, stance, dates, engagement, and source metadata were excluded as separate predictors.

method_claim: Label-blind quality rules and final external population
exact_protocol: Quality rules were fixed without using veracity outcomes. They applied whitespace/null normalization and excluded missing or artifact-only text, fewer than two alphabetic analyzer tokens after URL stripping for quality inspection, or fewer than 90% Latin letters. Case and punctuation were otherwise retained. The repository's English designation and script check did not establish complete language identification. The binary cohort contained 3,700 otherwise eligible items; exact source-overlap exclusions left 3,667 items, comprising 3,015 Fake and 652 Real.

method_claim: Exact overlap exclusions and approximate-match sensitivity
exact_protocol: Overlap screening compared each statement with source titles, bodies, and combined text, including source records ineligible for model training. Exact normalized-text matches or exact specific-resource URL matches with either source dataset were excluded from the primary clean target. URL checks used the existing offline normalization and included associated website and source review URLs; homepage-only matches did not count. Conservative lexical high-similarity matches were flagged rather than automatically excluded. All-eligible and clean-without-high-similarity targets were sensitivity scopes. Missing website files did not exclude an item, and offline screening could not resolve all redirects.

method_claim: Frozen model reuse, prediction timing, thresholds, and diagnostics
exact_protocol: The four frozen full-source natural LR/SVM models were reused without refitting. Target text and identifiers were fingerprinted before scoring, and all predictions were frozen before outcome labels were joined. Binary eligibility exposed membership only before prediction. LR probability and SVM score thresholds remained 0.5 and 0. Source comparisons used identical clean target rows. Representation diagnostics counted target unigram-token occurrences covered by the source vocabulary and rows with zero TF-IDF features, without double-counting bigrams. These were descriptive external evaluations, without a statistical winner test or target adaptation.

method_claim: Saved software versions, seeds, and reproducibility limits
exact_protocol: Classical and engagement analyses used the project's `.venv`: Python 3.14.2, NumPy 2.5.1, pandas 3.0.5, scikit-learn 1.9.0, SciPy 1.18.0, and statsmodels 0.15.0, as recorded in saved environment metadata. Transformer analyses used `.venv-transformer`, Python 3.12.7, PyTorch 2.14.0, and Transformers 5.17.0. Dependency pins and the immutable checkpoint revision were retained. Seed 42 governed primary random procedures where applicable; seeds 123 and 2026 were added only for the targeted stability check. MPS runs were seeded without asserting bitwise reproducibility across software or devices.

method_claim: Retained inputs, split integrity, and frozen evaluation artifacts
exact_protocol: Raw datasets were not modified. Processed records, stable UIDs, exclusion lineage, split manifests, selected configurations, scripts, model/checkpoint provenance, and aggregate outputs were retained. Where historical fingerprints were recorded, checksum comparisons supported artifact reuse, including split-manifest and source-configuration checks. For the original within-engagement run, recorded input and script hashes were verified, but historical output-file hashes were unavailable. The cross-context analysis fingerprinted the saved outputs at that stage and checked completion, convergence flags, standardized-mean identities, saved interval endpoints, and draw counts; it could not retrospectively verify original output checksums. Transfer configurations were locked before target scoring, and prediction records were frozen before evaluation-label joins. [Supplementary Methods S7](supplementary_methods_notes.md#s7-reproducibility-records) details the checksum limitation; the [protocol checklist](methods_protocol_checklist.csv) links methods to supporting artifacts.

method_claim: Bootstrap uncertainty versus descriptive predictive variation
exact_protocol: Engagement uncertainty was reported using overlap-cluster bootstrap percentile intervals, with independence and coverage assumptions stated explicitly. Fold and seed SDs described variability rather than confidence intervals. Text-model and external-source comparisons were descriptive predictive evaluations; no new inferential significance tests were used to declare model superiority, causal period differences, or causal lexical mechanisms.

subsection: S1. Content identity, lineage, and engagement linkage
method_claim: Final entity populations and provenance artifacts
exact_protocol: The authoritative CoAID populations are `A_primary_strict`, `B_resource_sensitivity`, and `C_high_certainty`, with 5,337, 5,205, and 5,082 entities, respectively. Their construction is recorded in `outputs/reports/coaid_version_aware_rebuild.md`, `outputs/tables/coaid_version_aware_entity_lineage.csv`, and `outputs/tables/coaid_version_aware_rebuild_metadata.json`. Specification A is the main population; B/C remain sensitivities.

subsection: S1. Content identity, lineage, and engagement linkage
method_claim: Version evidence and offline identity limitations
exact_protocol: Version partitions are the audited partitions, not clusters regenerated from a single similarity threshold. Supporting evidence includes normalized equality, token overlap, edit similarity, and body/abstract similarity, interpreted jointly with informative titles and metadata. Complete-link checks enforce compatible within-version pairs for material updates. Missing or insufficient excerpts do not establish identity, and an identical short introduction does not verify an entire historical webpage. Item-specific resource normalization remains offline; unverified redirects and cross-URL aliases are not inferred. The content-version evidence and final qualitative refinements are documented in `outputs/reports/coaid_content_version_stability.md` and its linked evidence artifacts.

subsection: S1. Content identity, lineage, and engagement linkage
method_claim: Representative record, entity UID, and ID union rules
exact_protocol: Within a final entity, the representative record is selected by descending stored body length, then descending title length, then release and original UID in ascending order. All original member captures remain in provenance. Entity UIDs incorporate the specific resource, aggregation mode, and sorted source UIDs. Post and reply IDs are set-unioned within the entity; legacy aggregate counts are not added together. These rules are implemented in `materialize` in `src/rebuild_coaid_version_aware_samples.py`.

subsection: S1. Content identity, lineage, and engagement linkage
method_claim: Exact linkage fields and FakeHealth mappings
exact_protocol: CoAID content IDs originate in `Unnamed: 0`; post files join through `index` and supply `tweet_id`, while reply files join through `news_id` and supply `reply_id`, within the release/file category. FakeHealth joins review/content/engagement records using `news_id` and retains unique IDs from the engagement dictionary's `tweets` and `replies` lists. Its separate `retweets` list is not included in the common primary count. Linkage implementations are retained in `src/build_coaid_content_table.py` and `src/build_fakehealth_content_table.py`.

method_claim: Design matrices and hurdle standardization helpers
exact_protocol: `src/run_version_aware_engagement_analysis.py` uses the validated count-fitting and standardization helpers in `src/run_primary_engagement_models.py` and `src/audit_engagement_estimand_robustness.py`. CoAID designs include an intercept, the Fake indicator, and first-recorded-release indicators with May as reference. FakeHealth uses the intercept and Fake indicator. For the hurdle, standardization averages each row's logistic probability multiplied by its conditional positive-count mean. Changing the reference indicator applies consistently to both model components.

method_claim: Deterministic component sampling and failure handling
exact_protocol: Bootstrap components are sampled with replacement without class stratification; each selected component contributes all its rows. Attempt seeds depend on the sample and attempt index rather than worker scheduling. Failed warm-start fits receive the documented multistart retry on the same draw. Failure, convergence, and successful-draw records are retained; inference targets 1,000 successful post refits. Each draw uses its own sampled reference distribution. The interval excludes uncertainty about family selection, unobserved social dependence, and content-identity decisions.

method_claim: Quantiles, dominant-component refits, and secondary diagnostics
exact_protocol: `src/run_cross_context_engagement_contrast.py` combines all marginal draw pairs and uses NumPy linear empirical quantiles. The dominant-component exclusion has its own 1,000-successful-refit CoAID bootstrap, combined with the saved FakeHealth draws. This exclusion distribution is distinct from conditioning the original bootstrap on draws omitting the component. Top-five and top-1% outcome exclusions are secondary point-estimate diagnostics; their separately retained HC0 intervals are not overlap-cluster confirmation. Reply NB fits remain provisional secondary summaries rather than a replacement primary outcome.

subsection: S3. Text grouping, quality, and source masking
method_claim: Exact and near-duplicate grouping thresholds
exact_protocol: Exact title/body comparisons use the minimally normalized case-preserved text. Near-duplicate screening uses case-preserving word shingles, ignoring punctuation for the comparison only: title bigram Jaccard >=0.95 for strings with at least 8 words, and body five-gram Jaccard >=0.90 with at least 30 words. Candidate filtering is followed by exact Jaccard verification, without learned TF-IDF or embedding features. Source lineage and specific-resource barriers are combined with text links into evaluation components. Cross-dataset flags cover directly matched rows and affected within-dataset groups; this screen does not claim to identify all paraphrases.

subsection: S3. Text grouping, quality, and source masking
method_claim: Final quality eligibility and preserved data lineage
exact_protocol: The final quality audit's `primary_modeling_eligible` flags supersede initial text-availability eligibility for modeling counts. All original records and decisions remain stored. Mixed artifact/substantive fields are reviewed without silently rewriting language; high-risk review-label disclosure is an exclusion rule. Primary split assignments are preserved when quality exclusions are applied. The applicable reports are `text_analysis_cohort_preparation.md` and `text_quality_and_source_cue_audit.md`; final sizes are corroborated by `tfidf_linear_svm_cohort_summary.csv`.

subsection: S3. Text grouping, quality, and source masking
method_claim: Saved CV membership and holdout choice rule
exact_protocol: The saved `outputs/splits/{coaid,fakehealth}_text_grouped_cv.csv` and corresponding `_text_holdout.csv` files define original UID assignments. `cv_fold=-1` is reserved holdout; training for fold f requires `cv_fold>=0` and `cv_fold!=f`, while validation uses `cv_fold==f`. Original ineligible rows have no usable training assignment. The candidate outer fold was chosen by minimizing summed absolute deviations from 20% of total, Fake, and Real counts, breaking ties by fold index. Quality filtering does not regenerate these partitions.

subsection: S3. Text grouping, quality, and source masking
method_claim: Label-blind source dictionary and transductive masking
exact_protocol: The source dictionary uses prepared publisher names, article hosts/URLs, and fixed metadata-activated aliases, without labels or engagement. Overlapping identifier spans are merged and replaced with `[SOURCE]`. Explicit URL hosts are masked while paths remain; selected ambiguous short names use case-sensitive matching. Evaluation metadata contributed to dictionary preparation, so masking is a transductive sensitivity. Masking can create identical strings across previously distinct groups through deliberate information removal; existing resource barriers remain unchanged.

subsection: S4. Classical tuning and selected settings
method_claim: Tokenization, intercepts, class weights, and tie distinctions
exact_protocol: Both vectorizers use the word-token pattern `(?u)\b\w\w+\b`, lowercase conversion, and no accent stripping. Intercepts are fitted with intercept scaling 1. In the pinned scikit-learn version, LR's pure L2 penalty is specified by `l1_ratio=0.0`. Balanced class weights depend on the training labels supplied to each fit. The mean-F1 and sample-SD tie tolerances are 0.001 for both classifiers; LR then uses unigram, smaller C, None weighting, larger min_df, and configuration ID. SVM omits the larger-min_df priority. The transformer tie policy differs: after the mean-F1 tolerance, its SD ordering has no additional tolerance.

subsection: S4. Classical tuning and selected settings
method_claim: Title eligibility and independently selected settings
exact_protocol: Title-only eligibility gives 1,645 FakeHealth items and 3,571 CoAID items; their holdouts contain 330 and 701 items. Comparisons with combined text use those same target rows. Natural-title settings are selected independently from combined-text settings, and masked-title fits reuse natural-title settings. Final selection tables and the corresponding baseline, SVM, and title-sensitivity reports retain these locks.

subsection: S4. Classical tuning and selected settings
method_claim: Lexical ranks and descriptive magnitude cutoffs
exact_protocol: For lexical alignment, absolute ranks use minimum rank for ties, with lexical order resolving top-N selection. The above-median subset strictly exceeds either model's absolute-coefficient median among shared terms. Near-zero coefficients satisfy absolute value <0.05; the descriptive meaningful-in-both category requires both absolute values >=0.05. These audit categories do not represent statistical significance or standardized causal effect sizes.

method_claim: Publisher identity normalization and platform accounts
exact_protocol: Names undergo Unicode NFKC normalization, case folding, and whitespace normalization. Hosts are lowercased and stripped of leading www; subdomains collapse only to an observed parent or audited identity host. Fixed aliases and unambiguous name-host links may join identities. Multiple attribution names on a host do not bridge unrelated hosts; conflicting audited identities and hosted tenants remain separate. Explicit Twitter/X account-status and YouTube channel/account URLs can define account proxies; generic platform hosts and unresolved routes do not.

method_claim: Nested partitions, support, and outer-fold selected settings
exact_protocol: The final FakeHealth outer and inner partitions use publisher/resource components, shuffled StratifiedGroupKFold, and seed 42. All outer test partitions meet the minimum support of 20 items per class, and all final inner partitions use three folds. The source map and component construction are frozen; no new normalization responds to model outcomes. Selected outer-fold natural configurations are: fold 0, (1,2)/min_df=5/C=1/balanced; fold 1, (1,1)/5/1/balanced; fold 2, (1,1)/2/1/balanced. The corresponding masked fits lock these natural settings.

method_claim: CoAID feasibility constraints
exact_protocol: Feasibility concerns in CoAID combine class-exclusive source families, sparse mixed-family data, and unresolved identities whose removal disproportionately excludes Fake support. The design therefore does not interpret a numerically feasible restricted partition as a clean language-generalization experiment. The full rationale and normalization rules are recorded in `publisher_heldout_feasibility.md`; the final experiment is `fakehealth_publisher_heldout.md`.

method_claim: Tokenizer, effective batch, scheduler, and checkpoint provenance
exact_protocol: The official fast tokenizer and checkpoint revision define pair special tokens; packing is checked against that template. All titles fit the available title budget in the evaluated cohorts. Training dynamically pads each microbatch and accumulates weighted gradients to the effective batch, retaining the partial final batch. The constant scheduler allows the epoch-2 candidate checkpoint to represent the same schedule as a two-epoch refit. Completed checkpoints retain model, optimizer, and random-state provenance; execution safeguards do not change the selected optimizer or predictor protocol.

method_claim: Locked selected configuration and paired seeds
exact_protocol: The primary experiment and token-budget follow-up are recorded in `distilroberta_text_experiment.md` and `distilroberta_budget_seed_stability.md`. The selected source settings are learning rate 2e-5 and three epochs. The targeted follow-up uses seeds 42, 123, and 2026 for both caps, reusing original seed-42 artifacts. Source class weights are recomputed for each fit's source-training population only; no target-label statistic enters training.

method_claim: External exact overlap, quality, and approximate thresholds
exact_protocol: For COVID-Rumor NEWS, quality screening strips URLs only when checking alphabetic tokens. Text normalization otherwise preserves case and punctuation. Exact statements are compared with source title/body/combined fields, including ineligible source records. Exact specific resources use the prior offline URL normalization, remove tracking parameters, retain path identity, and exclude homepage-only matches. Missing website files are retained. High-similarity flags use title bigram Jaccard >=0.95 with >=8 words, or body/combined five-gram Jaccard >=0.90 with >=30 words. Approximate matches are retained in the primary clean cohort unless they also meet an exact exclusion rule.

method_claim: External vocabulary coverage and zero-feature diagnostics
exact_protocol: Token occurrence coverage counts default-analyzer unigrams represented in the frozen source vocabulary; zero-feature diagnostics inspect transformed TF-IDF rows separately. Natural class prevalence and fixed decision thresholds are retained. The complete source-overlap evidence, quality rules, prediction-freeze checks, and evaluation scopes are recorded in `covid_rumor_external_transfer.md` and its companion validation JSON.

method_claim: Environment and protocol provenance hierarchy
exact_protocol: Saved protocol metadata provide software versions and input/output SHA-256 fingerprints. Classical versions are recorded in `engagement_model_run_metadata.json` and the classical model reports' `signature.versions` fields. Transformer versions and checkpoint identity are recorded in `transformer_feasibility.md`, `transformer_environment_audit.csv`, `requirements-transformer.txt`, and the final experiment metadata. The final experiment's saved settings take precedence over prospective feasibility proposals.

method_claim: Checklist, retained validations, and historical hash limitation
exact_protocol: The Methods protocol checklist links each main-text and supplementary block to its report, table, or exact implementation helper. Reproducibility checks cover cohort/UID identity, group separation, training-only fitting, locked configurations, prediction timing, convergence or finite-loss checks, and artifact integrity. The engagement contrast retains the documented limitation that the original within-engagement run lacked historical output-file hashes; later stages fingerprinted the saved outputs and checked their internal consistency without claiming a nonexistent earlier checksum. No raw datasets, prediction files, model checkpoints, or training logs were reopened to prepare these manuscript materials.
